outcomes.text: Understand factual information and abstract ideas in texts about general topics.
Understand formal and informal texts in a range of formats.
Understand varied grammatical structures, including some complex sentence forms.
Find and select relevant information and details from one or more longer texts.
Infer unknown words’ meanings from context across varied topics.
Understand a broad range of vocabulary on general subjects.
Recognise emotions, opinions and attitudes stated or strongly implied in texts.
Understand arguments and conclusions in discursive texts and distinguish fact from opinion.
Understand lengthy, complex texts and abstract ideas on general and specialised subjects.
Understand longer texts written in varied styles for diverse purposes.
Understand a wide range of complex grammatical structures.
Locate and select relevant details in longer texts across different genres.
Infer unfamiliar words and expressions from context across many topics.
Understand extensive vocabulary on general and specialised subjects.
Identify subtle details, attitudes and stated or implied opinions.
Understand arguments and conclusions in discursive texts and separate fact from opinion.
Communicate factual information, ideas, opinions and arguments about general subjects.
Communicate information, ideas, opinions and arguments about complex subjects.
Develop arguments with relevant supporting details and examples.
Develop and evaluate arguments, emphasising key issues and supporting viewpoints with reasons and examples.
Write detailed descriptions and narratives about real or imagined events and experiences.
Write assured, personal and natural descriptions and narratives of real or imagined experiences.
Organise ideas into coherent paragraphs and longer texts using cohesive devices.
Create fluent arguments, descriptions and narratives using linked paragraphs and varied cohesive devices.
Use register and style appropriate to the text’s purpose and genre.
Apply suitable register, style and genre conventions for the text’s purpose.
Use broad general-topic vocabulary with good accuracy.
Use extensive general and specialised vocabulary, including idioms, with high accuracy.
Use varied grammar, including some complex structures, with good accuracy.
Use varied complex grammatical structures with high accuracy.
Control spelling and punctuation effectively.
Produce writing with highly accurate spelling and punctuation.
Use depuis, il y a and voilà to express duration or how long something has been happening.
Use venir de to describe events that have just happened.
Distinguish future, vouloir, devoir and imperfect forms when translating meanings such as will, would, should and used to.
Form the passive voice in all tenses and recognise alternatives using on, nouns or reflexive constructions.
Use present and perfect subjunctive forms after expressions of desire, fear, emotion, judgement, possibility, obligation and doubt.
Use the subjunctive after conjunctions such as bien que, pour que and sans que.
Use dependent infinitives, including constructions with faire and laisser and after verbs of seeing, hearing or feeling.
Use infinitives after expressions including sans, pour, afin de, au lieu de and avant de, and in c’est pouvoir.
Invert the subject and verb when reporting speech.
Apply appropriate tenses when converting direct speech into indirect or reported speech.
Construct comparisons, including patterns such as il vaut mieux rester que de partir.
Use coordinating conjunctions such as car, donc, ensuite, et, mais, ou, puis and ou bien.
Use subordinating conjunctions including quand, où, parce que, si, puisque, comme and lorsque.
Choose appropriate tenses with quand, dès que and similar conjunctions to express logically future events.
Choose appropriate tenses in si clauses.
Use prepositions for place, including chez, entre, devant, à côté de, près de and en face de.
Use prepositions for time, including avant, après, pendant, pour, dans and en.
Use prepositions expressing movement, including jusqu’à and vers.
Use other prepositions such as contre, malgré, sans, sauf and selon.
Select the correct preposition with verbs such as penser, croire and jouer.
Use de after indefinite expressions when followed by an adjective.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers accurately.
Use expressions of quantity such as assez, trop, demi, moitié, peu, tant and autant.
Express dates, years and times, including using the 24-hour clock.
Use tout correctly as an adjective, noun and adverb.
Use toujours to express always, continuation, still or at any rate.
Express dimensions, distances, prices and rates accurately.
Read varied literary texts independently.
Read varied literary texts fluently, appreciating implicit meanings and ideas.
Write about literary themes, characters, ideas and details while recognising genre conventions.
Organise literary ideas into coherent paragraphs and longer texts.
Organise literary responses clearly using coherent paragraphs and appropriate terminology.
Develop arguments using relevant supporting details and textual examples.
Develop and support evaluations of important themes and ideas with detailed textual examples.
Give a personal response, explaining what is appreciated and why.
Give a clear personal interpretation, explaining reactions to themes and characters.
Explain language choices and identify features that prompt reader responses.
Analyse language choices and evaluate how they engage the reader.
Critically evaluate themes, characters, ideas and details while appreciating genre conventions.
Explore popular entertainment, its role in life, and celebrity culture including role models and responsibilities.
Explore how identity is expressed and how cultural heritage, sites, festivals and traditions are preserved and respected.
Explore the arts, access and funding, awards, representation and diversity.
Explore sport, physical and mental health, exercise, diet, sleep, self-esteem and healthcare provision.
Explore work–life balance, leisure activities and relaxation.
Discuss friendships, family, relationships, generational differences and changing family patterns.
Consider quality of life, living environments, urban and rural differences, overcrowding and social isolation.
Explore lifestyle choices involving relationships, diet, fashion, self-expression, values and personal goals.
Explore diets, eating habits, food production’s environmental impact, food ethics, labelling and government intervention.
Understand global warming, climate change, pollution, solutions, government action and economic effects.
Explore biodiversity and ecosystem protection, including the treatment of animals.
Consider the effects of population growth.
Examine natural-resource use, recycling, waste disposal, consumerism and overconsumption.
Understand fossil fuels, renewable energy, energy geopolitics and local environmental effects of energy production.
Explore ways to reduce environmental impact through individual housing, food and travel choices.
Explore education systems, student issues, school organisation and school’s preparation for future life.
Explore access, barriers, costs, benefits and alternatives such as vocational education, apprenticeships and gap years.
Explore careers, workplaces, working practices, employment, unemployment, job satisfaction, volunteering and charity work.
Understand inclusivity, diversity, gender equality and social mobility.
Explore social prejudices including ageism, racism and classism.
Examine immigration, refugee experiences and integration.
Understand social organisation, law and order, governance at local and national levels, and communities.
Explore national and global citizenship.
Examine the rights and responsibilities of individuals and governments.
Consider sustainable tourism and the benefits of travel.
Examine global cooperation and its tensions with national priorities.
Compare individual, industrial and governmental roles, including environmental movements.
Explore medical advances and ethical issues in scientific research.
Understand smart technology, privacy and security concerns.
Explore artificial intelligence.
Consider digital media, including its benefits and dangers.
Understand communication technology.
Explore online communities.
Consider access to technology.
Explore the use of technology in education.
Explore the use of technology in the workplace.
